stem: Shamrao's income in 2015-16 after paying all taxes is 6,40,000 rupees. He pays 2000 rupees per month for insurance and 20% of his annual income into his provident fund. He puts aside 500 rupees per month for emergencies. How much money does he have for yearly spending ?
solution:
(i) Annual income = 6,40,000 rupees
(ii) Insurance premium = \(2000 \times 12 = 24{,}000\) rupees
(iii) Contribution to provident fund = \(6{,}40{,}000 \times \dfrac{20}{100} = 1{,}28{,}000\) rupees
(iv) Amount put aside for emergency = \(500 \times 12 = 6000\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Total planned expenditure = \(24{,}000 + 1{,}28{,}000 + 6{,}000 = 1{,}58{,}000\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Amount available for yearly expenses = \(6{,}40{,}000 - 1{,}58{,}000 = 4{,}82{,}000\) rupees

stem: Mr. Shah invested 3,20,000 rupees in a bank at 10% compound interest. He also invested 2,40,000 rupees in mutual funds. At market rates he got 3,05,000 rupees after 2 years. How much did he gain ? Which of his investments was more profitable ?
solution:
(i) We shall first calculate the compound interest on the money invested in the bank.
Compound interest = Amount \(-\) Principal
That is, \(I = A - P = P\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^{n} - P = P\left[\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^{n} - 1\right]\)
\(= 3{,}20{,}000\left[\left(1 + \dfrac{10}{100}\right)^{2} - 1\right] = 3{,}20{,}000\left[(1.1)^{2} - 1\right] = 3{,}20{,}000\,[1.21 - 1]\)
\(= 3{,}20{,}000 \times 0.21 = 67{,}200\) rupees
Mr. Shah invested 3,20,000 rupees in the bank and got 67,200 rupees as interest.
Percentage of interest = \(\dfrac{100 \times 67200}{3{,}20{,}000} = 21\)
\(\therefore\) The investment in the bank gave a profit of 21%.
(ii) The amount Mr. Shah got at the end of 2 years from the mutual fund = 3,05,000 rupees
\(\therefore\) The gain from the mutual fund = \(3{,}05{,}000 - 2{,}40{,}000 = 65{,}000\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Percentage gain = \(\dfrac{65000 \times 100}{2{,}40{,}000} = 27.08\)
The investment in the mutual fund yielded a profit of 27.08%.
It is clear that Mr. Shah's investment in the mutual fund was more profitable.

stem: Mr. Shaikh invested 4,00,000 rupees in a glass industry. After 2 years he received 5,20,000 rupees from the industry. Putting aside the original investment, he invested his gains in a fixed deposit and in shares in the ratio 3 : 2. How much amount did he invest originally in each of the schemes ?
solution:
Mr. Shaikh's profit at the end of 2 years = \(5{,}20{,}000 - 4{,}00{,}000 = 1{,}20{,}000\) rupees
Amount invested in the fixed deposit = \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times 1{,}20{,}000 = 3 \times 24{,}000 = 72{,}000\) rupees
Amount invested in shares = \(\dfrac{2}{5} \times 1{,}20{,}000 = 2 \times 24{,}000 = 48{,}000\) rupees
Mr. Shaikh invested 72,000 rupees in the fixed deposit and 48,000 rupees in shares.

stem:
The ratio of Mr. Anil's monthly income to expenditure is 5 : 4. For Mr. Aman the same figure is 3 : 2. Also, 4% of Aman's monthly income is equal to 7% of Anil's monthly income. If Anil's monthly expenditure is 96,000 rupees -
(i) Find Aman's annual income.
(ii) Savings made by Mr. Anil and Mr. Aman.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the printed stem reads "If Anil's monthly EXPENDITURE is 96,000 rupees", but the book's own solution below sets \(5x = 9600\) from "Anil's monthly income is 9600 rupees", and the printed answers (Aman's income 16,800; Anil's saving 1,920) follow only from that reading. The stem is wrong in both the quantity (expenditure for income) and the magnitude (96,000 for 9,600). Read it as "Anil's monthly INCOME is 9,600 rupees".]

We know that savings = Income \(-\) Expenditure.
Anil's income to expenditure is 5 : 4, so suppose Anil's income is \(5x\) and his expenditure is \(4x\).
Aman's income to expenditure is 3 : 2, so suppose Aman's income is \(3y\) and his expenditure is \(2y\).
Anil's monthly income is 9600 rupees, \(\therefore 5x = 9600\), \(\therefore x = 1920\).
Monthly expenditure \(= 4x = 4 \times 1920 = 7680\) rupees.
Anil's monthly expenditure is 7680 rupees, \(\therefore\) Anil's saving is 1920 rupees.
4% of Aman's income = 7% of Anil's income
\(\therefore \dfrac{4}{100} \times 3y = 9600 \times \dfrac{7}{100}\)
\(\therefore 12y = 9600 \times 7\)
\(\therefore y = \dfrac{9600 \times 7}{12} = 5600\)
Aman's income \(= 3y = 3 \times 5600 = 16{,}800\) rupees
Aman's expenditure \(= 2y = 2 \times 5600 = 11{,}200\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Aman's savings \(= 16{,}800 - 11{,}200 = 5{,}600\) rupees
Aman's monthly income is 16,800 rupees and Aman's saving is 5,600 rupees.
Anil's monthly saving is 1,920 rupees.

stem:
Mr. Mhatre is 50 years old. His gross total income is 12,00,000 rupees. He has invested the following amounts in different schemes.
(i) Insurance premium : 90,000 rupees
(ii) Investment in provident fund : 25,000 rupees
(iii) Investment in PPF : 15,000 rupees
(iv) National Savings Certificate : 20,000 rupees
Find out the permissible deductions, taxable income, and the income tax payable.
solution:
(1) Total yearly income = 12,00,000 rupees.
(2) Total savings under section 80C.

| Savings | Amount of savings (rupees) |
|---|---|
| (i) Insurance premium | 90,000 |
| (ii) Provident Fund | 25,000 |
| (iii) Public Provident Fund | 15,000 |
| (iv) National Savings Certificate | 20,000 |
| Total | 1,50,000 |

According to section 80C, a maximum deduction of 1,50,000 rupees is permissible.
(3) \(\therefore\) Taxable income = Amount in [1] \(-\) Amount in [2] \(= 12{,}00{,}000 - 1{,}50{,}000 = 10{,}50{,}000\)
(4) We shall use Table I to calculate Mr. Mhatre's total income tax.
Mr. Mhatre's taxable income = 10,50,000 rupees, which is greater than ten lakh rupees.
\(\therefore\) According to Table I, income tax = \(1{,}12{,}500 + 30\%\) (of total income minus 10 lakh)
\(\therefore 10{,}50{,}000 - 10{,}00{,}000 = 50{,}000\)
\(\therefore\) Income tax \(= 1{,}12{,}500 + 50{,}000 \times \dfrac{30}{100} = 1{,}12{,}500 + 15{,}000 = 1{,}27{,}500\)
We must also include 2% education cess and 1% secondary and higher education cess.
Education cess \(= 1{,}27{,}500 \times \dfrac{2}{100} = 2550\) rupees
Secondary and higher education cess \(= 1{,}27{,}500 \times \dfrac{1}{100} = 1275\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Total income tax \(= 1{,}27{,}500 + 2550 + 1275 = 1{,}31{,}325\) rupees
Mr. Mhatre's tax payable = 1,31,325 rupees.

stem: Mr. Ahmed, a 62 year old senior citizen, is employed in a private company. His total annual income is 6,20,000 rupees. He has contributed 1,00,000 rupees to the Public Provident Fund and paid a premium of 80,000 rupees for the year for health insurance and a donation of 10,000 rupees to CM's Relief Fund. What is tax payable ?
solution:
(1) Total yearly income = 6,20,000 rupees
(2) Total deduction (according to 80C)
(i) Public Provident Fund = 1,00,000 rupees
(ii) Insurance = 80,000 rupees
Total = 1,80,000 rupees
(iii) Section 80C permits a maximum deduction of 1,50,000 rupees.
(3) Amount given to CM's Relief Fund (according to 80G) = 10,000 rupees.
(4) Taxable income = (1) \(-\) [(2) + (3)] \(= 6{,}20{,}000 - [1{,}50{,}000 + 10{,}000] = 4{,}60{,}000\) rupees
From Table II we see that the taxable income is in the slab 3 lakh to 5 lakh rupees.
\(\therefore\) Income tax \(= (\text{Taxable income} - 3{,}00{,}000) \times \dfrac{5}{100} = (4{,}60{,}000 - 3{,}00{,}000) \times \dfrac{5}{100} = 1{,}60{,}000 \times \dfrac{5}{100} = 8000\) rupees
Education cess is levied on income tax.
Education cess \(= 8{,}000 \times \dfrac{2}{100} = 160\)
Secondary and higher education cess \(= 8{,}000 \times \dfrac{1}{100} = 80\)
\(\therefore\) Total income tax \(= 8000 + 160 + 80 = 8240\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Tax payable by Mr. Ahmed is 8,240 rupees.

stem: Mrs. Hinduja's age is 50 years. Last year her taxable income was 16,30,000 rupees. How much income tax has she to pay ?
solution:
Mrs. Hinduja's taxable income is in the bracket of 10,00,000 rupees and above.
Let us use Table I to compute her income tax. Accordingly, for income greater than 10,00,000 rupees :
Income tax = \(1{,}12{,}500 + 30\%\) of total income minus ten lakh
Mrs. Hinduja's income minus ten lakh \(= 16{,}30{,}000 - 10{,}00{,}000 = 6{,}30{,}000\) rupees
From Table I,
Income tax \(= 1{,}12{,}500 + 6{,}30{,}000 \times \dfrac{30}{100} = 1{,}12{,}500 + 30 \times 6{,}300 = 1{,}12{,}500 + 1{,}89{,}000 = 3{,}01{,}500\) rupees
On this we compute
1% secondary and higher education cess \(= \dfrac{1}{100} \times 3{,}01{,}500 = 3015\) rupees
2% education cess \(= \dfrac{2}{100} \times 3{,}01{,}500 = 6030\) rupees
\(\therefore\) Total income tax payable \(= 3{,}01{,}500 + 3015 + 6030 = 3{,}10{,}545\)
\(\therefore\) Total income tax payable is 3,10,545 rupees.

stem: For different types of investments what is the maximum permissible amount under section 80C of income tax ?
_why: Section 80C caps the total deduction for savings and investments at 1,50,000 rupees. The chapter's own solved examples use this ceiling twice: Mr. Mhatre's savings total exactly 1,50,000 and are allowed in full, while Mr. Ahmed's total 1,80,000 and are cut back to 1,50,000.

context: Write the correct alternative answer for each of the following questions.
stem: A person has earned his income during the financial year 2017-18. Then his assessment year is ....
_why: Income is earned in the financial year and assessed in the year that follows it, so income of the financial year 2017-18 is assessed in 2018-19. Option C is the financial year itself, and options A and D are earlier years.
